title: Exact cohomology ladder for the internal-Hom filtered-colimit comparison
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen universe, with $\mathcal O$ commutative [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Put $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and use its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal M)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix the functorial K-injective target models for $H(A,N)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(A,N)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models]. For any small filtered diagram $N:I\to\operatorname{CoCh}(\mathcal M)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], put $N_\infty=\varinjlim_iN_i$ termwise and let $\alpha_A:\varinjlim_iH(A,N_i)\to H(A,N_\infty)$ be the image in $D(\mathcal M)$ of the canonical complex cocone map on these models. All colimits here are termwise sheaf colimits. For every small filtered complex diagram $(K_i)$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, there is a natural isomorphism
$$H^q(\varinjlim_iK_i)\cong\varinjlim_iH^q(K_i).$$
Consequently termwise filtered colimits preserve quasi-isomorphisms and common cohomological lower bounds. Let $A\xrightarrow u B\xrightarrow v C\xrightarrow w A[1]$ be any distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the sequences
$$\cdots\to\varinjlim_iH^{q-1}(H(A,N_i))\to\varinjlim_iH^q(H(C,N_i))\to\varinjlim_iH^q(H(B,N_i))\to\varinjlim_iH^q(H(A,N_i))\to\varinjlim_iH^{q+1}(H(C,N_i))\to\cdots$$
and
$$\cdots\to H^{q-1}(H(A,N_\infty))\to H^q(H(C,N_\infty))\to H^q(H(B,N_\infty))\to H^q(H(A,N_\infty))\to H^{q+1}(H(C,N_\infty))\to\cdots$$
are exact, and form a commuting ladder whose vertical arrows at $X=A,B,C$ are $H^q(\alpha_X)$ under the displayed cohomology-colimit identification. The arrows in both rows are those induced by precomposition with $u,v,w$; for $w$ one uses the signed source-shift comparison $H(A[1],N)\cong H(A,N)[-1]$ (cochain convention $K[n]^q=K^{q+n}$, $d_{K[n]}=(-1)^nd_K$), which on the Hom-complex models reindexes components and multiplies degree-$q$ components by $(-1)^q$, independently of $N$. Commutativity includes every connecting square, with these specified signs. No boundedness, continuity or constructibility assumption is imposed on $A,B,C$ or $N$.

proof.text: Use the independent-universe Grothendieck-abelian module-sheaf theorem and the adopted source instance for preservation of exact colimits by complex homology. This proves ladder_filtered_cohomology. Naturality of preservesColimitNatIso conjugates the cohomology map of a colimit of objectwise quasi-isomorphisms to the colimit of an objectwise isomorphism. A colimit of a diagram of zero cohomology objects is zero, and preservesColimitIso transports this to the homology of the complex colimit, proving the common-lower-bound clause.

proof.text: Evaluate the localized strict-colimit functor and its canonical comparison from lem-sfb-rhom-colimit-source-transport at the fixed target diagram N. Its normalized component equation is precisely the equation defining ladderStrictAlpha. The actual localization factorization coefficientHomResolutionIso is natural in the target, so gives an isomorphism of diagrams of derived Hom objects. Apply cohomology, take colimits, and compose with the inverse canonical cohomology-colimit isomorphism. This defines beta, whose equation on every injection follows from the two canonical cocone equations. Testing beta followed by H(alpha) on each injection reduces to naturality of coefficientHomResolutionIso and the colimit.desc equation. No new object is selected from a mere existence statement.

proof.text: Fix a derived target M and use lem-coef-signed-derived-internal-hom-exact. Compose this contravariant exact Hom functor with degree-q cohomology. Apply its homological exactness to T, T.rotate and T.rotate.rotate. The normalized inverse shift at opposite degree -1 is exactly sourceShift(X,1). Together with the cohomology shift isomorphism it identifies H^(q-1)(Hom(X,M)) with H^q(Hom(X[1],M)). Its naturality transports the first two objects of the twice-rotated sequence. The rotated first arrow is negative precomposition with u[1]; negating the first transporting isomorphism absorbs this sign. The three resulting exact spots have exactly ladderPrecomp and ladderBoundary, with their fixed signed normalization.

proof.text: The row maps are natural transformations in the target. Their objectwise zero-composite equations therefore give short complexes in the diagram category. Homology is pointwise there, so their objectwise exactness implies exactness in that category. Exact filtered colimits preserve these short complexes, yielding all three exact spots of the colimit row. For any target-natural transformation f, composing its colimit-map/vertical-desc square with an injection reduces exactly to f.naturality at Q(iota_i). This proves both precomposition squares and the signed boundary square without an additional long-exact-sequence naturality theorem.

Steps 1–3: exactness of filtered colimits from lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian (same hypotheses) gives the colimit complex, ker d_∞ = colim Z and im d_∞ = colim B, so H^q(colim) = colim H^q, naturally, with θ∘ι_i = H^q(leg). Quasi-isomorphisms and common lower bounds are preserved. Step 4: source quasi-isomorphism invariance of the internal Hom complexes into K-injective targets comes from lem-pur-rhom-well-defined-universes with s = id, then step 3 for the colimit, so F, G and a descend through the localisation; no colimit of K-injectives is used. Step 5: I rechecked by hand the sign of s, (s^n f)^p = (−1)^n f^{p−1}, against the def-pur-hom-complex differential and d_{K[−1]} = −d_K; both sides give (−1)^{n+1} d_J f^{p−1} − f^p d_P^p, and s commutes with postcomposition and with termwise colimits.
